title: Oskar and the missing necklace (paraphrase)
topic: A detective named Oskar investigates the theft of a necklace from a jewellery shop; a clerk remembers a stranger, muddy tracks lead into an alley, a delivery man confesses, Oskar solves the case before midnight
tail_E: The stolen necklace alone is worth a fortune, for it is made of pure
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'gold' is the natural completion of 'a necklace worth a fortune ... made of pure' in the jewellery-theft context; it does not occur in the units or the tail (no 'gold', 'golden', 'Gold'). ' gold' is a single Pythia token (id 5328); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.73, next candidate 'silver' ~ 0.04).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring, paraphrase of family F12
notes: Formulation B: independent re-phrasing of the ten F12A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Oskar). Replacements include investigates a theft at a small jewellery shop/takes on a theft case at a jeweller's (untersucht einen Diebstahl/übernimmt einen Fall von Diebstahl, in einem Juweliergeschäft/bei einem Juwelier), owner describes the necklace in detail/shopkeeper describes the necklace very precisely (Besitzer beschreibt Halskette/Ladenbesitzer schildert Kette), display case stands open behind the counter/glass cabinet is open behind the sales counter (Vitrine steht offen/Glasschrank ist offen, Theke/Tresen), clerk remembers a stranger/salesman mentions a stranger (erinnert sich an/erwähnt), finds muddy footprints near the back door/discovers muddy tracks by the rear door (findet Fußspuren/entdeckt Spuren), trail leads into an alley/tracks run into a side street (Spur führt/Spuren verlaufen), two neighbours hear strange noises/some neighbours notice odd sounds (hören/bemerken), questions the clerk a second time/interrogates the salesman once more (befragt/verhört), delivery man admits the theft/courier owns up to the theft (Lieferant gesteht/Kurier bekennt sich zu), solves the case before midnight/wraps up the case just before midnight (löst/klärt). 'übernimmt', 'verhört' and 'bekennt sich' are inseparable; 'zugeben' and 'aufklären' were avoided because they are separable. Present tense and positive polarity throughout.
